title: Matching maps of a local acyclic fibration are generalized covers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves and [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] for simplicial sets. For $V\in\mathcal C$, put $h_V(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(W,V)$. The simplex $\Delta^n$ is represented by $[n]$, its boundary $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of its proper faces (empty when $n=0$), and $\Lambda_i^n$ is the union of the faces other than face $i$, for $n\ge1$ and $0\le i\le n$. Let $F,G:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$ be objectwise Kan simplicial presheaves. A map $f:F\to G$ is a local Kan fibration if every commutative square from $h_V\times\Lambda_i^n\to h_V\times\Delta^n$ to $f$ has fillers after restriction along every arrow in some covering sieve of $V$; the fillers need not agree for different arrows. For objectwise Kan $F,G$, call $f$ a local weak equivalence if it induces an isomorphism on the associated sheaves of $\pi_0$ and, for each $V\in\mathcal C$, $x\in F(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, an isomorphism on the associated sheaves on $\mathcal C/V$ of $\pi_m(F|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(G|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$, where $\mathcal C/V$ has the induced topology. Suppose that $f$ is both a local Kan fibration and a local weak equivalence. For $n\ge0$, let $\widetilde M_nF$ be the presheaf of sets whose value at $V$ is the set of simplicial maps $\partial\Delta^n\to F(V)$, and define $\widetilde M_nG$ in the same way. Then the induced map of presheaves of sets
$$F_n\longrightarrow\widetilde M_nF\times_{\widetilde M_nG}G_n$$
is a generalized cover [def-cbc-generalized-cover]. Here $F_n(V)=F(V)_n$; in degree zero the boundary is empty and this is the map $F_0\to G_0$.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen Proposition 3.2 and equation (3.4), v2 HTML lines 293-339.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$ and $V\in\mathcal C$. A section of $\widetilde M_nF\times_{\widetilde M_nG}G_n$ at $V$ is exactly a pair $(a,b)$ with $a:\partial\Delta^n\to F(V)$, $b:\Delta^n\to G(V)$ and $f_Va=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$. Indeed an $n$-simplex $z$ of a simplicial set $Z$ is the simplicial map $\Delta^n\to Z$ sending an operator $\alpha:[q]\to[n]$ to $Z(\alpha)(z)$; evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_{[n]}$ is the inverse correspondence. Under this correspondence the displayed relative matching map sends $z$ to $(z|_{\partial\Delta^n},f_Vz)$. Thus it suffices to find strict extensions of each $(a,b)$ locally on $V$.

source.place: DHI Proposition 3.2 and equation (3.4), printed pp. 7-8; direct simplex evaluation identifies the lifting problem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-local-weak-equivalence-homotopy-lifting] to $(a,b)$. Its Kan hypotheses are the assumed objectwise Kan conditions, and its homotopy-sheaf hypotheses are exactly the assumed local weak equivalence, including every basepoint and the slice-site topology. Obtain a covering sieve $S$ on $V$. For each $u:W\to V$ in $S$ choose $c:\Delta^n\to F(W)$ extending $u^*a$, and a homotopy $H:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to G(W)$ from $f_Wc$ to $u^*b$, constant on the boundary. We will straighten this particular homotopy after further covering restrictions of $W$.

source.place: Theorem 6.15(a) and the locally fibrant paragraph in Proposition 7.2, printed pp. 14-15; DHI Proposition 3.1.

proof.text:
Here is the finite prism decomposition needed for straightening; it is a calculation with simplices, not an appeal to an anodyne-closure theorem. Put $P=(\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1)\cup(\Delta^n\times\{0\})$. The $q$-simplices of $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ are weakly increasing strings in the product poset $[n]\times[1]$. Every strict string extends to a maximal chain, and all maximal chains are
$$\sigma_k=((0,0),\ldots,(k,0),(k,1),\ldots,(n,1)),\quad 0\leq k\leq n.$$
Adjoin these $(n+1)$-simplices to $P$ in order $\sigma_n,\sigma_{n-1},\ldots,\sigma_0$. For $\sigma_k$, a face $d_j\sigma_k$ with $j\ne k,k+1$ omits a spatial vertex and so lies in the boundary prism. The face $d_{k+1}\sigma_k$ is in the bottom when $k=n$, and is $d_{k+1}\sigma_{k+1}$ when $k<n$, hence already present. In contrast $d_k\sigma_k$ contains all spatial vertices, is not in the bottom, and is contained in no previously adjoined $\sigma_l$ with $l>k$: it includes $(k,1)$ whereas such chains do not. Its proper faces lie in the other faces of $\sigma_k$. Thus each intersection with the preceding union is exactly $\Lambda_k^{n+1}$, and adjoining $\sigma_k$ is a single horn pushout. After the $n+1$ attachments the union is the whole prism. For $n=0$ this is the one horn $\{0\}=\Lambda_0^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$.

source.place: Proposition 7.2, locally fibrant paragraph, referencing Corollary 4.2: explicit finite prism calculation of the homotopy-straightening inclusion.

proof.text: Over $W$, define a map $P\to F(W)$ by $c$ on the bottom and $(u^*a)\operatorname{pr}_1$ on the boundary prism. They agree on their intersection, so the degreewise union gives a simplicial map. Its composite with $f_W$ equals $H|_P$ by the four identities in Step 2. Apply the local Kan hypothesis horn by horn along Step 3. More precisely, let $P_0=P\subseteq P_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq P_{n+1}=\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ be that filtration and let $R_j$ be the sieve of arrows $r:W'\to W$ for which the given square admits a lift on $P_j$. It is a sieve because any such lift restricts further, and $R_0$ is maximal. If $R_j$ covers, choose a partial lift for each $r$ in $R_j$. The next horn square, with base map $r^*H|_{\sigma_{n-j}}$, has fillers on a covering sieve $T_r$ of $W'$ by the definition of local Kan fibration. Gluing a filler to the partial lift works because their intersection is precisely that horn. Hence $r^*R_{j+1}$ contains $T_r$ and covers. Upward closure of covering sieves follows directly from transitivity: for covering $T\subseteq T'$, every pullback of $T'$ along an arrow in $T$ is maximal. Transitivity applied to $R_j$ now makes $R_{j+1}$ cover. This finite induction yields a covering sieve of $W$ on each arrow of which $H$ has a lift $\widetilde H$ extending the prescribed map on $P$. No compatibility between different arrows is used. Restricting $\widetilde H$ to the endpoint $1$ gives $z:\Delta^n\to F(W')$ with boundary the restriction of $a$ and with $f_{W'}z$ equal to the restriction of $b$.

source.place: Proposition 7.2, locally fibrant paragraph, printed p. 15; finite horn-by-horn lifting and covering-sieve transitivity written out instead of the reference to Corollary 4.2.

proof.text: Let $R$ be the lifting sieve of $(a,b)$ for the relative matching map, in the sense of [def-cbc-generalized-cover]. For every $u:W\to V$ of the covering sieve $S$ of Step 2, Step 4 supplies a covering sieve contained in $u^*R$. Upward closure makes $u^*R$ covering, and transitivity makes $R$ covering on $V$. As $V$ and $(a,b)$ were arbitrary, this is exactly the generalized-cover conclusion. If $n=0$, the map $a$ is unique because the boundary is empty; the same one-horn argument yields local preimages of every vertex of $G$, proving the asserted degree-zero case $F_0\to G_0$.

source.place: DHI equation (3.4), printed p. 8, and definition of generalized cover on p. 7; transitivity completes the local lifting argument.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 7.2, locally fibrant paragraph, expanded using Theorem 6.15(a); the finite prism filtration and every sieve refinement are proved explicitly. DHI Proposition 3.2 and equation (3.4) identify the matching formulation. Both papers read online; archival copies WANTED.
